#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

If kube manager is started with no cloud-provider, it looks like the service-lb-controller fails to be instantiated but its handlers are added to the informer on instantiation. A part of its initialization happens on the Run method. because the recorder is nil, the event handler will panic. 

The event handler shouldn't be registered. It is detected with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/50c12437604b0cd5a73514389409fc2fde8b91bd. I open another PR to fix it, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128182

This PR removes the event recorder from event handlers.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->
Fixes #128121

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

```release-note
Fixes a bug in the `k8s.io/cloud-provider/service`  controller, it may panic when a service is updated because the event recorder was used before it was initialized. All cloud providers should using the `v1.31.0` cloud provider service controller must ensure that the controllers is initialized before the informer start to process events or update it to the version 1.32.0.
```

@aojea The last question is whether we can initialize the recorder variable in `Run` function instead of `New` function. If yes, other changes can be reverted. Most controllers in `pkg/controller` package are using the `New` function to initialize the recorder variable.

The problem with the event recorder is that it runs (sic!) goroutines. That makes initializing it in the `Run` method more suitable because then there is a proper context for those goroutines (cancellation!).

What was problematic with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/50c12437604b0cd5a73514389409fc2fde8b91bd was that it left the event recorder as field in the controller struct. Usage of that field in the event handler then became a runtime problem instead of a compile-time error.

If I were to do this again, I would probably remove the recorder field and turn it into a parameter of the functions called by `Run`.

> The problem with the event recorder is that it runs (sic!) goroutines. That makes initializing it in the `Run` method more suitable because then there is a proper context for those goroutines (cancellation!).

Contextual logging depends on constructing the recorder with a context passed in by the caller. Also, cancellation.

>  as @carlory says most of the intree controllers are initializing them in the constructor 

That's only because that's old code that hasn't been updated yet. The constructor for the event recorder hid the fact that it spawns goroutines. An API that allows passing a context for that was added later.

> > That's only because that's old code that hasn't been updated yet.
> Can I pick it up?

Yes, please do.

My initial reaction was "let's combine with other upcoming changes once the new client-go APIs are available", but I don't know how many of this will be relevant for controllers (`logcheck` will tell us, I just haven't looked yet) and a single PR making exactly one change may be simpler to review.

If the controller removed the event recorder field, it would become harder for callers to get the recorder. These functions have to accept a recorder as an argument, which is a bit annoying. Or put the recorder into the context in the `Run` function and pass the generated context to children functions. When a child function needs to record an event, it has to get the recorder from the context like logger.

```golang
func (c *Controller) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
	logger := klog.FromContext(ctx)

	eventBroadcaster = record.NewBroadcaster(record.WithContext(ctx))
	eventRecorder = eventBroadcaster.NewRecorder(scheme.Scheme, v1.EventSource{Component: "service-controller"})
	ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, "eventRecorder", eventRecorder)

	defer runtime.HandleCrash()
	defer c.serviceQueue.ShutDown()
	defer c.nodeQueue.ShutDown()

	// Start event processing pipeline.
	eventBroadcaster.StartStructuredLogging(0)
	eventBroadcaster.StartRecordingToSink(&v1core.EventSinkImpl{Interface: c.kubeClient.CoreV1().Events("")})
	defer eventBroadcaster.Shutdown()

	logger.Info("Starting controller")
	defer logger.Info("Shutting down controller")
}

func (c *Controller) sync(ctx context.Context, key string) error {
	logger := klog.FromContext(ctx)
	eventRecorder := ctx.Value("eventRecorder").(record.EventRecorder)

	// Record the event
	eventRecorder.Eventf(nil, v1.EventTypeNormal, "Synced", "Successfully synced %s", key)
}
```

Is it desired?

issue_context.title: Crash on kube manager's service-lb-controller after v1.31.0
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

If kube manager is started with no `cloud-provider`, it looks like the service-lb-controller is instantiated but not started. However, part of its initialization happens on the `Run` method **and** its handlers are added to the informer on instantiation. So the handlers still run and it crashes when they do because there is stuff not initialized, like in this case, the event recorder:
